title: Root Cause: Why Attaching Tracers to Rebuilt Models Fails
text: Name. No nesting, no sense of what called what, and the tool calls, the actual work, never appeared in the trace at all. Useless for the one question tracing exists to answer, what happened? The cause is the interesting part. The tracer was attached to the model, but the code builds a fresh model on every single call. title: Results: 92 Nested Observations & Full Tool Call Visibility
text: Showing the real call tree. And for the first time, the tool calls are in there. Same run, finally [clears throat] legible. The lesson, trace the run, not the model, especially when the model gets rebuilt on every call. Attach your observability once at the top, and name it something you can actually find later. title: Key Takeaway: Trace the Run, Not the Model
text: Up as one trace, or as a scatter of disconnected ones? If it's scattered, find where the handler is attached and ask whether that object gets rebuilt on every call. That's usually the whole bug. One brief, one trace. Trace the run, not the model. Humanitarian's AI.
